builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TwinCheck: Evidence-Grounded Negative-Twin Verification for Stateful Tool Agents
summary: TwinCheck replaces blind or suspicion-based intervention on agent tool calls with an inference-time policy that intervenes only when a trace-local evidence condition holds, constructing a counterfactual 'negative twin' replacement that must pass structural checks and a pairwise order-symmetric verifier before substitution. It costs extra verifier model calls per candidate intervention, added trace-logging and exact-replay infrastructure for evaluation, and engineering complexity in defining evidence conditions and structural checks; there is no training or fine-tuning cost, so it fits a 24 GB GPU or API-only budget. It can fail when the verifier prefers a flawed twin, when evidence conditions misfire on out-of-distribution traces, and its evidence base is narrow: one benchmark, one model family, and 159 paired tasks.
rationale: The gain is a real but modest absolute improvement demonstrated on a single small benchmark with API models, so the technique is cheap enough to adopt at small scale but requires validation on the reader's own tool-use workload before production reliance.
technique: Evidence-gated counterfactual verification of tool calls

claims.statement: TwinCheck replaces blind or suspicion-based intervention on agent tool calls with an inference-time policy that intervenes only when a trace-local evidence condition holds, constructing a counterfactual 'negative twin' replacement that must pass structural checks and a pairwise order-symmetric verifier before substitution. It costs extra verifier model calls per candidate intervention, added trace-logging and exact-replay infrastructure for evaluation, and engineering complexity in defining evidence conditions and structural checks; there is no training or fine-tuning cost, so it fits a 24 GB GPU or API-only budget. It can fail when the verifier prefers a flawed twin, when evidence conditions misfire on out-of-distribution traces, and its evidence base is narrow: one benchmark, one model family, and 159 paired tasks.

Task success on 159 multi-turn BFCL V4 tasks rises from 45.3% to 58.5% for GPT-5.6 Sol (95% CI [8.2, 18.8]), an absolute gain of 13.2 points with no observed success-to-failure regressions; this is a point gain, not a multiplicative factor.
